samples.text:
The diagram shows the process of making hard cheese. There are eight stage, from collecting milk to packaging.

Firstly, fresh milk is delivered from dairy farms. Then the milk is pasteurised, it is heated to 72°C for 15 seconds and then cooled. After that, culture and rennet are added to the milk and it begin to set.

Next, the milk separate into solid curd and liquid whey. Then the curd is cut into cubes and heated, and the whey is drained off. After this, the curd is salted and it is pressed into the moulds.

In the ripening stage, the cheese is stored at 10°C for 3–24 months. This is the longest stage in the process. Finally, the cheese is cut, wrapped and labelled, so it can be sold in the shops.

Overall, making hard cheese is a linear process with many steps. The milk become cheese through heating, cutting, salting and a long time of ripening, and this is why it takes a lot of time.
samples.why: Basic overview split between start and end · stages and figures reported accurately · mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary · agreement errors and a comma splice that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates the various stages involved in the production of hard cheese.

Overall, it is a linear process consisting of eight stages, starting with the collection of fresh milk and finishing with the packaging of the cheese. The ripening stage is by far the longest, lasting up to two years, while pasteurisation takes only a few seconds. The whole process, therefore, can take a long time to complete.

To begin with, milk is delivered from dairy farms and pasteurised, which involves heating it to 72°C for 15 seconds before it is cooled. Culture and rennet are then added, causing the milk begin to set, and it soon separates into solid curd and liquid whey.

After this, the curd is cut into cubes and heated, while the whey is drained off. This means that the curd, rather than the whey, is used to make the cheese. The curd is then salted and pressed into moulds. Next, the cheese is left to ripen at a temperature of 10°C for a period of between 3 and 24 months. In the final stage, it is cut, wrapped and labelled so that it is ready to be sold.
samples.why: Clear overview with the key feature highlighted · figures accurate and well integrated · logical progression with passive forms · less common vocabulary (pasteurised, ripen) · one grammar slip.

samples.text:
The diagram outlines the sequence of steps by which fresh milk is transformed into packaged hard cheese.

There are eight stages in total, beginning with the delivery of milk and ending with packaging, and it combines heating, cutting and pressing with a long period of controlled storage. Of the stages for which a duration is given, ripening is by far the most time-consuming, lasting anywhere from three months to two years, whereas pasteurisation takes a matter of seconds.

Initially, milk is transported from dairy farms, after which it is pasteurised by being heated to 72°C for just 15 seconds and then cooled. Culture and rennet are subsequently introduced, prompting the milk to set, and it separates into solid curd and liquid whey.

The curd is next cut into cubes and heated, and the whey is drained off, so that only the solid part is carried forward. It is then salted and pressed into moulds. Following this, the cheese is ripened at a cool 10°C for between 3 and 24 months. Finally, it is cut, wrapped and labelled for sale, at which point the product is ready to leave the production line.
samples.why: Skilfully selected overview contrasting stage durations · figures used precisely for comparison · cohesion managed well · precise vocabulary (prompting, time-consuming) · wide range of structures, error-free.
